course: AP Macroeconomics - Scarcity, Stabilisation and the Open Economy
attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
description: The whole-economy view: scarcity and market fundamentals, national income and price determination, the financial sector, stabilisation policy and its long-run consequences, and the open economy.

concepts.title: Scarcity and opportunity cost
concepts.summary: Every choice costs the next-best alternative forgone, so scarcity is about trade-offs rather than a temporary shortage.

concepts.title: Production possibilities curve
concepts.summary: The frontier shows the maximum output combinations and the opportunity cost of moving along it.

concepts.title: Comparative advantage and gains from trade
concepts.summary: Specialising where the opportunity cost is lowest raises total output, which is why voluntary trade can benefit both sides.

concepts.title: Marginal analysis and decision rules
concepts.summary: A rational decision compares the marginal benefit of one more unit with its marginal cost, not the totals.

concepts.title: Demand and the law of demand
concepts.summary: Quantity demanded falls as price rises, holding every other influence constant.

concepts.title: Supply and the law of supply
concepts.summary: Quantity supplied rises as price rises because a higher price makes production more profitable at the margin.

concepts.title: Market equilibrium and disequilibrium
concepts.summary: Price settles where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied; a mismatch shows up as a surplus or a shortage.
prerequisites: Demand and the law of demand
Supply and the law of supply

concepts.title: Determinants of demand and supply
concepts.summary: Non-price influences shift the curves, and a shift moves equilibrium price and quantity together.

concepts.title: Consumer and producer surplus
concepts.summary: Surplus measures the gain from trade: what buyers would have paid above price, and what sellers would have accepted below it.

concepts.title: Market efficiency and deadweight loss
concepts.summary: Total surplus is maximised at equilibrium, so any move away from it destroys some surplus as deadweight loss.

concepts.title: Price ceilings and price floors
concepts.summary: A binding ceiling creates a shortage and a binding floor creates a surplus, because neither changes the underlying curves.

strands.strand: Economic Indicators and the Business Cycle

concepts.title: Gross domestic product
concepts.summary: GDP is the market value of final goods and services produced inside a country during a period.

concepts.title: Real versus nominal GDP
concepts.summary: Deflating nominal GDP by a price index separates a change in output from a change in prices.

concepts.title: Limitations of GDP as a measure
concepts.summary: GDP omits unpaid work, inequality, environmental cost and leisure, so it measures production rather than welfare.

concepts.title: Economic growth and productivity
concepts.summary: Long-run living standards rise with productivity, which depends on physical capital, human capital and technology.

concepts.title: Unemployment: measurement and types
concepts.summary: Frictional, structural and cyclical unemployment are distinguished by their cause, and only some respond to demand policy.

concepts.title: Labour force participation
concepts.summary: Participation measures the share of the working-age population working or seeking work, and it moves with the cycle.

concepts.title: Inflation and the consumer price index
concepts.summary: A price index tracks the cost of a fixed basket, and its percentage change is the inflation rate.

concepts.title: Costs of inflation
concepts.summary: Expected inflation is manageable, but unanticipated inflation redistributes wealth between borrowers and lenders.
prerequisites: Inflation and the consumer price index

concepts.title: Business cycle phases
concepts.summary: Expansion, peak, contraction and trough describe the recurring but irregular pattern of output and employment.

concepts.title: Aggregate demand
concepts.summary: AD slopes downward because a lower price level raises real wealth, lowers interest rates and raises net exports.

concepts.title: Shifts in aggregate demand
concepts.summary: Spending shocks shift AD, and how much output changes depends on the slope of short-run aggregate supply.

concepts.title: Short-run aggregate supply
concepts.summary: SRAS slopes upward because some input prices and wages are sticky in the short run.

concepts.title: Long-run aggregate supply
concepts.summary: LRAS is vertical at potential output, set by productive capacity rather than the price level.

concepts.title: Macroeconomic equilibrium and output gaps
concepts.summary: Where AD meets SRAS gives short-run output, and the distance from LRAS signals inflationary or recessionary pressure.

concepts.title: Fiscal policy: spending and taxation
concepts.summary: Government shifts aggregate demand directly through spending and indirectly through taxes and transfers.

concepts.title: The spending multiplier
concepts.summary: An initial spending change produces a larger total change because each round of income is partly re-spent.

concepts.title: Automatic stabilizers
concepts.summary: Taxes and transfers that vary with income dampen the cycle without any new legislation.

concepts.title: Crowding out
concepts.summary: Deficit spending can raise interest rates and displace private investment, reducing the net stimulus.

concepts.title: Supply-side fiscal policy
concepts.summary: Policies aimed at incentives can raise potential output rather than merely shifting demand.

concepts.title: Functions and measures of money
concepts.summary: Money is a medium of exchange, a unit of account and a store of value, and M1 and M2 measure it by liquidity.

concepts.title: Banking and money creation
concepts.summary: Banks create deposits by lending out reserves, so the money supply exceeds the monetary base.

concepts.title: The money multiplier
concepts.summary: Maximum deposit expansion is the reciprocal of the reserve ratio, and it shrinks with leakage into cash.

concepts.title: Money demand and the money market
concepts.summary: Money demand depends on income and interest rates, and equilibrium sets the short-term interest rate.

concepts.title: The loanable funds market
concepts.summary: The real interest rate balances saving with investment demand, linking the financial and goods markets.
prerequisites: Money demand and the money market

concepts.title: Central banks and monetary policy tools
concepts.summary: Open-market operations, reserve requirements and the administered rate change reserves and short-term interest rates.

concepts.title: Transmission of monetary policy
concepts.summary: A rate change works through investment, consumption and net exports, and it arrives with a lag.
prerequisites: Central banks and monetary policy tools

concepts.title: Interest rates and investment
concepts.summary: Lower real interest rates raise the present value of future returns, so investment spending rises.

concepts.title: The short-run Phillips curve
concepts.summary: The short-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment arises from sticky prices and surprise inflation.

concepts.title: The long-run Phillips curve
concepts.summary: In the long run the trade-off disappears: unemployment returns to its natural rate whatever the inflation rate.

concepts.title: Expectations and credibility
concepts.summary: Once expectations adjust, only surprise inflation moves output, so central-bank credibility has real value.

concepts.title: Monetary policy in the long run
concepts.summary: Money is neutral in the long run: it affects the price level rather than real output.

concepts.title: Fiscal policy in the long run
concepts.summary: Persistent deficits can crowd out capital formation and shift the burden toward future taxpayers.

concepts.title: Deficits, debt and sustainability
concepts.summary: Sustainability depends on the gap between the interest rate and the growth rate, not on the debt level alone.
prerequisites: Fiscal policy in the long run

concepts.title: Policies to promote growth
concepts.summary: Policies that raise saving, investment, human capital and technology raise long-run potential output.

strands.strand: Open Economy: International Trade and Finance

units.unit: Trade and the balance of payments

concepts.title: Balance of payments accounts
concepts.summary: The current account and the financial account offset each other, so a trade deficit is matched by net capital inflow.

concepts.title: Trade barriers and their effects
concepts.summary: Tariffs and quotas raise domestic prices, reduce imports and destroy some surplus as deadweight loss.

prerequisites: Trade and the balance of payments

concepts.title: Exchange rates and the foreign exchange market
concepts.summary: The exchange rate is the price of one currency in another, set by the supply of and demand for currencies.

concepts.title: Determinants of exchange rates
concepts.summary: Interest-rate differentials, relative inflation and trade flows move currency demand and supply.
prerequisites: Exchange rates and the foreign exchange market

concepts.title: Appreciation, depreciation and net exports
concepts.summary: A weaker currency makes exports cheaper abroad, which raises net exports and shifts aggregate demand.

concepts.title: Open-economy policy linkages
concepts.summary: With mobile capital, monetary and fiscal policy work differently under fixed and floating exchange-rate regimes.
